ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

New perceptual symptoms

A 17-year-old taking prescribed amphetamine for ADHD begins hearing voices and believes classmates are monitoring his thoughts. There is no fever or focal neurologic deficit. He has no previous psychotic symptoms. Which response is most appropriate?

  1. Continue unchanged until the next annual review
  2. Add a second stimulant without reviewing the first
  3. Promptly assess the psychotic symptoms and reconsider the stimulant, including discontinuation
  4. Increase the stimulant dose because attention has worsened
  5. Assume the symptoms prove lifelong schizophrenia
Answer and explanation

Promptly assess the psychotic symptoms and reconsider the stimulant, including discontinuation

Stimulants can produce new psychotic symptoms even at recommended doses; the new symptoms need assessment rather than automatic dose escalation.

Option explanations

Promptly assess the psychotic symptoms and reconsider the stimulant, including discontinuation: Stimulants can produce new psychotic symptoms even at recommended doses; the new symptoms need assessment rather than automatic dose escalation.

Increase the stimulant dose because attention has worsened: Escalation may aggravate a medication-related psychiatric reaction.

Assume the symptoms prove lifelong schizophrenia: Medication effects and other causes must be evaluated before assigning that conclusion.

Continue unchanged until the next annual review: New psychotic symptoms require timely assessment.

Add a second stimulant without reviewing the first: This increases exposure without addressing the adverse-effect concern.
